title: dedicated-autoscaler: improve burst throughput controls and utilization reporting
author: Sophie Nguyen
title_and_description: Summary: Improve Dedicated autoscaler burst controls and make utilization reporting more accurate and actionable for fleet operators. Motivation: customers running Redwood Dedicated reported burst throttling leading to degraded tail throughput under spiky traffic. Existing token-bucket smoothing and queue-length heuristics underreport real GPU utilization during bursts, making capacity planning and autoscaler tuning difficult. This PR updates the autoscaler to (1) add a burst throughput guardrail that accounts for sustained KV cache pressure and active inflight tokens, (2) smooth token-bucket refill to reduce oscillation while preserving short burst capacity, and (3) enhance utilization metrics emitted to the ops pipeline so rolling-window and per-model utilization are visible for fleet-level reporting. Changes are backwards-compatible for autoscaler configs: new fields are optional and default to safe values. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-3421) - [x] Unit & integration tests added - [x] Metrics dashboard updated - [x] Load test run against staging fleet - [x] Docs/update notes drafted
commits: feat(autoscaler): add burst_throughput_guardrail and kv_cache_pressure tracking
perf(autoscaler): smooth tokenbucket refill algorithm and add configurable alpha parameter
feat(metrics): emit per-fleet and per-model rolling_window_utilization metrics
test(autoscaler): unit tests for guardrail and smoothing behavior
docs: add autoscaler config reference and upgrade notes
diff_highlights: services/autoscaler/policy/tokenbucket.go: implemented exponential moving average (EMA) based refill smoothing (alpha configurable); default alpha=0.25
services/autoscaler/policy/guardrail.go: new guardrail that reduces allowed burst throughput when kv_cache_pressure > 0.65 or inflight_token_ratio > threshold
observability/metrics/emitters/utilization_emitter.py: added rolling_window_utilization and per_model_utilization tags, emits 1m/5m/15m windows
services/autoscaler/core/manager.go: integrate guardrail checks into scaling decision path and add telemetry points for decision rationale
review_conversation: Carlos Mendes: Overall LGTM. A few nits around metric cardinality and log verbosity. Please ensure per-model tags aren't too high-cardinality in high-tenant setups.
Sophie Nguyen: Good call - limited per_model tag to top-N active models per fleet and added sampling for lower-priority tags. Updated tests to assert tag constraints.
Priya Shah: Concern about default alpha=0.25 being too aggressive; can we validate on canary before bumping in prod?

Sophie Nguyen: Agreed. Added canary gating config and an override in defaults.yaml. Also added results from staging load tests showing tail latency improved by ~12% at 95th percentile with minimal impact to cost.
Jordan Lee: Noted a race in manager.go where guardrail evaluation could read stale inflight counts; added mutex in follow-up commit. Re-running CI.
Taylor Brooks: Observability/alerting owners - updated dashboard and added alert 'DedicatedAutoscaler.SustainedBurstUtilization' with recommended threshold. Please review thresholds before rollout.
Carlos Mendes: Approved after minor test cleanup and adding one integration test for model-tag sampling.
ci_checks: ci/integration: passed (load test: burst scenario) - results attached
load_test_summary: Staging load tests ran a 30-minute burst scenario (100x baseline qps spike). Results: 95p tail latency reduced 12%, average GPU utilization smoother during bursts, autoscaler stabilizes faster (median recovery 45s -> 28s). Tokenbucket smoothing reduced oscillation events from 18 to 4 in the timeframe.
upgrade_notes: New optional autoscaler config fields: burst_throughput_guardrail {enabled:boolean, kv_pressure_threshold:float, inflight_ratio_threshold:float} and tokenbucket_refill {alpha:float}. Defaults are safe; for most fleets no action required. To enable canary, set autoscaler.canary.mode=staged and configure percent_of_fleet. See docs/ops/autoscaler-config.md
release_notes: Improved Dedicated autoscaler: added burst throughput guardrails and smoothing to reduce oscillation during spikes; enhanced utilization metrics for fleet-level reporting. No breaking changes; new config fields are optional.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: overly aggressive smoothing could reduce effective burst capacity causing short tail regressions. Mitigation: canary gating, default conservative alpha, staging load tests, and rollback flag. Observability: new telemetry exposes decision rationale to ops for quick diagnosis.
manual_steps_after_merge: 1) Deploy autoscaler service with new config defaults to canary pool for 24h. 2) Monitor DedicatedAutoscaler.SustainedBurstUtilization, per-model utilization dashboards, and rollback if sustained tail latency > baseline+10%. 3) After canary validation, flip canary.mode to off to rollout fleet-wide.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: All new fields are optional. Existing fleets will continue to operate with previous behavior. The tokenbucket smoothing defaults match pre-change steady-state refill to avoid behavior shift unless explicitly configured.
final_merge_message: Squash merged by Sophie Nguyen - Added burst throughput guardrail, tokenbucket smoothing, and richer utilization metrics. Load tests show improved tail latency and reduced oscillation. Config fields optional and gated by canary.
human_readable_summary: This PR strengthens Dedicated autoscaler's burst handling and observability: a guardrail prevents uncontrolled bursts when KV cache pressure is high, tokenbucket refill smoothing reduces autoscaler oscillations, and new utilization metrics make fleet-level capacity planning more accurate. Changes are opt-in and canary-gated to minimize risk.
